sites.name: NAS ATLANTA

facts.summary: DeKalb County commissioners voted 6-1 on Nov. 18, 2025 to approve a $45 million Sky Harbour hangar development on about 12.8 acres on the east side of DeKalb-Peachtree Airport (PDK). The plan is eight hangars under a 50-year ground lease with no county appropriation. The county projects a $576 million financial impact over the lease term, including $66 million in direct ground-lease revenue to PDK. This is an approval, not a report that construction has begun.
facts.reference: DeKalb County news: BOC approves hangar development at PDK (item dated Dec. 1, 2025)
facts.quote: On Tuesday, Nov.18, in a 6-1 vote, the DeKalb County Board of Commissioners approved a $45 million development

facts.summary: The county names Sky Harbour as the developer, described as a home-based operator for business aircraft at PDK. AvWeb reports the board advanced the 'Sky Harbour Group' development, so the printed entity name differs between sources. The exact legal entity was not confirmed.
facts.reference: DeKalb County news: BOC approves hangar development at PDK (item dated Dec. 1, 2025)
facts.quote: by Sky Harbour, a home-based operator for business aircraft at DeKalb-Peachtree Airport (PDK),

facts.summary: After the approval, residents raised noise and environmental-pollution concerns about the PDK hangar expansion at a Dec. 9 town hall. Commissioner Ted Terry proposed a moratorium on all new hangar development until the PDK master plan is updated, plus an FAA ban on night flights except for emergencies. The article reports these as proposals.
facts.reference: Rough Draft Atlanta: residents upset over PDK expansion (Dec. 10, 2025)
facts.quote: a moratorium on all new hangar development until the PDK master plan is updated

gaps: Matched on the airport identity: the FUDS record is the former Naval Air Station Atlanta, which is now DeKalb-Peachtree Airport. The atlas's 412 acres is smaller than the airport footprint, and the project is 12.8 acres (county) or 13 acres (AvWeb). The match is by airport name, not by parcel.

Sky Harbour's Request for Proposals 22-500625 (Eastside Aviation Development on PDK, issued Aug. 2022) and the April 2024 Operations Committee recommendation of Sky Harbour as sole proposer were found only in search snippets. The county PDF links returned HTTP 404, so they are not cited.
Operations Committee agendas and minutes from 2024 and 2025 show the item continuing. The county PDFs for those returned HTTP 404 and are not cited.
The Chamblee citywide data center moratorium (Urbanize Atlanta, July 2026) is not about PDK and is not cited. Whether PDK sits inside Chamblee city limits was not verified.
Not verified: the pending FAA approval and the groundbreaking target of Q3 2027 that appear in an AIN search snippet, because the AIN page was not opened.
Only one council-level opposition item was opened. The Ted Terry proposal is cited as a proposal, and its outcome was not found.

sites.name: CP GORDON
gaps: Searched 'CP Gordon', 'Camp Gordon' with Chamblee, Atlanta, DeKalb and development terms. No news found on a current project at the Camp Gordon WWI site near Chamblee.

Search results were unrelated Chamblee projects: Chamblee City Center, Marlowe Chamblee (Greystar, March 2025), Chamblee Park (Toll Brothers), and The Frazier at Olde Towne Gordon. None names Camp Gordon or this site.

Historical background only, not cited as news: Camp Gordon was a WWI training camp in Chamblee, abandoned in 1921. DeKalb County bought land from the former camp in 1940 for an airport, which became DeKalb-Peachtree Airport. The CP Gordon atlas point is about 0.6 mile from PDK, so it may be part of the same former camp footprint; this is not confirmed.
